points.title: How this chat assistant works
points.content:
This chat is a custom-built retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system, not a generic chatbot. It lives in src/lib/chat-knowledge.ts and a Next.js API route at /api/chat.

Pipeline per message:
1. Browser POSTs the conversation history to /api/chat (Vercel serverless function).
2. Upstash Redis rate-limits per visitor IP — sliding window of 10 sends per 60s. Returns HTTP 429 with a friendly fallback if exceeded.
3. Input is validated (message count cap of 20, per-message length cap of 4000 chars, total bytes cap of 50k).
4. A guardrail layer blocks off-topic queries and private-data probes using a regex blocklist plus an allow-list of public topics derived from portfolio.json.
5. For predictable openers (project rundowns, common suggested questions), the route returns a deterministic canned response — no LLM call, no quota burn.
6. For genuine follow-ups, a small in-memory keyword retriever scores each knowledge section against the query: +4 per keyword match, +1 per body-text match. Top 7 sections become the LLM's grounded context.
7. The route calls Google's Gemini API, walking a fallback chain (gemini-2.5-flash → gemini-2.0-flash → gemini-2.5-flash-lite → gemini-1.5-flash). Each model has its own free-tier daily quota, so chaining four stacks the effective ceiling to roughly 4250 requests per day at no cost.
8. The system prompt instructs the model to use only the provided context and refuse to invent details.

Stack:
- Frontend: React 19 + Tailwind in a custom 'terminal' panel inside the bentOS dashboard.
- API: Next.js 16 App Router route handler on Vercel serverless functions.
- LLM: Google Gemini Flash family via plain REST (no SDK, to keep the worker bundle small).
- Rate limiting: @upstash/ratelimit on top of Upstash Redis (free tier).
- Retrieval: deterministic keyword scoring over portfolio.json + projects/*.json + talking-points/*.json. No embeddings, no vector DB — overkill for ~50 sections and would cost money.

Why keyword retrieval instead of embeddings? Speed, determinism, zero cost, and the corpus is tiny and well-categorized. Embeddings would be the right call if there were thousands of documents or fuzzy semantic matching mattered, but for a portfolio chatbot the structured fields (project names, technologies, talking-point keywords) make exact-token matching very effective.

Why a fallback chain instead of one model? Each Gemini free-tier model has its own daily quota; chaining four means a single visitor would have to send thousands of messages before the chat fully degrades to demo mode. Auth errors fail fast (the same key wouldn't work on a different model); rate limit and server errors retry against the next model in the chain.
